title: In Vitro Reconstitution of the Actin Cytoskeleton Inside Giant Unilamellar Vesicles
protocol: Prepare the aqueous Inner Non-Polymerization (INP) Buffer in a total volume of 5 mL by mixing specified components.
Add proteins to the INP buffer at 4 °C to prepare the Protein Mix (PM).
Form an F-actin layer by adding gelsolin, cofilin, and VCA-His to the PM.
Prepare a control experiment with fluorescent dye instead of PM.
Prepare the aqueous Inner Polymerization (IP) Buffer in a total volume of 5 mL by mixing specified components.
Mix INP buffer containing PM and IP buffer at a volume ratio of 1:1 to prepare the Final Buffer (FB).
Prepare the aqueous Outside Buffer (OB) in a total volume of 150 µL by mixing specified components.
Add 100 µL of 25 mg/mL L-α-phosphatidylcholine into a glass vial.
Evaporate chloroform with argon gas to leave a dry lipid film at the bottom of the vial.
Mix EPC with DOGS-NTA-Ni at a 10:1 ratio before evaporating chloroform.
Add 2 mL of mineral oil and sonicate the lipid-oil mixture for 1 hour at room temperature.
Store the lipid-oil mixture at 4 °C for up to one week, re-sonicating before use if necessary.
Draw 100 µL of lipid-oil mixture into a plastic tube.
Add 10 µL of final buffer (FB) to the lipid-oil mixture and form a droplet.
Aspirate the FB droplet and lipid-oil mixture up and down with a glass syringe multiple times.
Repeat aspiration until a whitish and cloudy emulsion is formed.
Put 30 µL of OB in a separate plastic tube.
Place 30 µL of the lipid-oil mixture on top of OB and let it sit for ~10 mins to develop a lipid monolayer at the interface.
Carefully add 50 µL of the FB/oil emulsion to the top oil phase of the tube from step 2.3.
Centrifuge the plastic tube at 100 x g for 15 minutes at 4 °C.
Vary time and centrifugation speed to optimize for liposome formation.
Carefully remove the oil phase away by pipette.
Aspirate extra volume if needed, ensuring not to put the pipette tip at the side of the tube to avoid creating a meniscus of oil on top of the liposome phase.
With a new pipette, slowly stick the pipette tip into the remaining bottom phase and aspirate the aqueous volume to collect liposomes.
Pour 100 µL of OB into the well of an incubation chamber (4-well plate containing 12 mm round coverslips).
Gently deposit the collected liposomes into OB.
Place another coverslip on top of the chamber.
Observe liposomes with a confocal microscope using a 63x oil-immersion objective.
Use 488 nm, 647 nm, and 561 nm laser lines to observe fluorescently labeled lipid, encapsulated fluorescent dye, and encapsulated fluorescently labeled actin, respectively.
Capture frames of interest and save images in TIFF format.
Open the TIFF file using ImageJ/Fiji software.
Go to Image > Adjust > Brightness/Contrast.
Adjust brightness and contrast by adjusting Minimum and Maximum settings, and Brightness, Contrast sliders.
Click on the Rectangle selection tool and select the region of interest (ROI).
Go to Image > Crop to crop the ROI.
Go to Analyze > Set Scale.
Enter 1.0 in the Pixel Aspect Ratio field and set μm as the Unit of Length.
In the Distance in Pixels field, enter the image width in pixels.
In the Known Distance field, enter the real image width in microns.
Using the Oval selection tool, draw a circle along the edge of the liposome.
Go to Analyze > Measure to measure the area of the circle, from which the diameter of the liposome can be calculated.
